question.text: Ankit Desai runs a 'value-style' PMS but notices several cheap stocks are cheap because earnings are collapsing. Which risk is he facing?

explanation.text: The Logic: Value traps = stocks that screen cheap on multiples but are genuinely deteriorating (structural decline, accounting issues). Low P/E is a signal of problems, not mispricing. The Trap: Momentum crash = sharp reversal in trending stocks; growth reversal = re-rating of growth names downward — different dynamics. Cross-Exam Context: XV Ch 10 covers qualitative overlays to avoid value traps. Manager's Pro-Tip: Combine value screens with governance, cash-flow quality, and trend-of-earnings filters — pure multiples will draw you into traps every cycle.
